question: In its resolution of 15 December 2011 on detention conditions in the EU, Parliament reaffirmed ‘the importance of granting specific protection to mother detainees and to their children including through the use of alternative detention in the child’s best interest’, and called on ‘Member States and the Commission to actively promote and support such initiatives’.

There are cases in Belgium that violate the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child and reinforce the doubts about the country’s intention to comply with its international obligations. In the light of the above: 1.
Is the Commission aware of such cases where the rights of the mother have not been protected and mother detainees have been separated from their children?
Does it intend to take measures to prevent these blatant human rights violations from happening again in Belgium?
answer: The right to respect for private and family life and the rights of the child are protected respectively in Article 7 and 24 of the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights and the Commission is committed to ensuring the respect of the Charter within the remit of its competences. According to its Article 51(1), the Charter applies to Member States only when they are implementing EU law.

The issue raised by the Honourable Member does not as such constitute implementation of EU law. In such cases, it is for Member States, including their judicial authorities, to ensure that fundamental rights are effectively respected and protected in accordance with their national legislation and international human rights obligations, including the United Nations Convention on the rights of the child.

Additionally, on 8 December 2022, the Commission adopted a recommendation on the procedural rights of suspects and accused in pre-trial detention and material detention conditions (1). The recommendation contains specific guidance as regards the protection for mother detainees and their children (2).
The topic of detention is also a priority for the Belgian Presidency and Council conclusions on small-scale detention will be adopted in June 2024.

Commission Recommendation (EU) 2023/681 of 8 December 2022 on procedural rights of suspects and accused persons subject to pre-trial detention and on material detention conditions, C/2022/8987, OJ L 86, 24.3.2023, p. 44-57. Member States should inform the Commission on their follow-up to this recommendation within 18 months of its adoption.
Based on this information, the Commission will monitor and assess the measures taken by Member States and submit a report at the end of 2024. See paragraphs 64-66 of the recommendation.
